_beaker_view_readme: Optional 'beaker_view' field on a reaction (see content/reactions/*.json) describes what a student would actually SEE happen in a beaker/test tube — grounded in NCERT and standard chemistry, never guessed. Omit the whole field entirely for a reaction with no meaningful visual change (e.g. esterification — the defining cue is smell, not sight) or one that isn't something a student observes directly (e.g. haber-process — industrial-scale, all gases, no beaker). Fields: initial_appearance/final_appearance (plain-prose colour + solid-present description, matching the chapter content's voice — not a controlled vocabulary); gas_evolution.occurs (bool) + .vigor ('vigorous'|'moderate'|'gentle', null iff occurs is false) + .colour (hex string, null unless the gas has a specific, notably-coloured appearance — e.g. brown NO2 fumes, pale yellow-green chlorine — leave null for an ordinary colourless gas so the renderer falls back to its default translucent-white bubble); precipitate.forms (bool) + .colour (string, null iff forms is false — a surface deposit from a metal-displacement reaction, e.g. copper plating onto zinc, is NOT a precipitate, describe that in final_appearance instead); thermal.effect ('exothermic'|'endothermic'|'neither' — 'neither' for anything electrically-driven like electrolysis, or where no reaction-specific thermal observation is actually taught) + .visually_obvious (bool — true only for steam/visible heat/light, NOT just 'feels warm to the touch') + .visual_cue (string describing that visible cue, null iff visually_obvious is false — including when the cue text would only explain why nothing is visible, e.g. 'kept cool to avoid a visible temperature rise'; that belongs in explanation/observation instead, not as a visual_cue) ; observation (one line, present tense, concrete — the same voice as a chapter's section body, e.g. 'the ribbon fizzes vigorously and dissolves quickly'). If you're not confident of a specific colour or vigor, say so inside the field's own text (see lead-copper-chloride's beaker_view for an example) rather than omitting the field or guessing silently — a flagged uncertainty is useful, a wrong colour stated as fact is not.
_beaker_view_animation_readme: Optional 'animation' sub-object inside beaker_view — the per-reaction parameters the scene renderers in components/reaction-animation/ draw from (a reaction with a beaker_view but no animation shows an 'animation unavailable' card). Every colour and visible effect must come from the reaction's own prose fields or NCERT; if neither describes a visible change, leave it out rather than inventing one. Fields: type ('combustion'|'metal_water'|'gas_evolution'|'electrolysis'|'thermal_decomposition'|'photolytic'|'precipitation'|'temperature_change'|'displacement'|'dissolution'|'surface_change'|'colour_change') picks the scene; apparatus ('beaker'|'test_tube'|'test_tube_burner'|'electrolysis_cell'|'flame'|'dish'); solution ({from, to} hex, or null for no liquid); solid ({from, to, shape} — to null means used up; shape 'strip'|'granules'|'lump'; or null); gas ({colour: hex or null for colourless, amount: 'none'|'little'|'some'|'lots'} — a coloured gas is drawn as a cloud filling the vessel, a colourless one as bubbles); temperature ('hot'|'cold'|'none' — draws a thermometer rising/falling; only set it where the prose or NCERT says the change is noticeable); intensity ('slow'|'steady'|'violent'); precipitate (hex or null); flame ({colour, smoke: hex or null, fuel: 'gas_jet'|'wick'|'solid'|'mixture'}, combustion only); electrolysis ({cathode, anode: {gas, colour, volume}, collect}, electrolysis only); effects (optional list of 'steam'|'glow'|'sparks'|'flash'|'floats'|'darts'|'soot'|'condensation', each one backed by the prose or NCERT).

reaction.explanation: Acetic acid reacts with sodium bicarbonate to form sodium acetate, water and carbon dioxide.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Two colourless liquids: vinegar (dilute acetic acid) and a white sodium bicarbonate powder or solution, no solid metal involved.
beaker_view.final_appearance: Still a colourless solution once the fizzing stops; the bicarbonate is fully consumed.
beaker_view.observation: Adding vinegar to baking soda sets off a brisk, immediate fizz of carbon dioxide bubbles, and the mixture feels slightly cool to the touch as it reacts.

steps.title: Attack on aromatic ring
steps.explanation: The electrophile attacks the electron-rich benzene ring, forming a sigma complex.
steps.key_point: The aromaticity is temporarily lost in this step.

question.prompt: What is the hybridization of carbon in ethyne (C2H2)?
question.explanation: Each carbon in ethyne forms 2 sigma bonds and 2 pi bonds, so it is sp hybridized.

_cbse_question_readme: CBSE board-paper question bank, separate from the 'question' shape above. Files: content/questions/class10/<chapter_id>.json, one per NCERT Class 10 chapter, where chapter_id is the id of the matching Class 10 topic file in content/topics/ (chemical-reactions-and-equations, acids-bases-and-salts, metals-and-non-metals, carbon-and-its-compounds, periodic-classification-of-elements). Each file is { chapter_id, class, topic_file, source_note, questions: [cbse_question, ...] }, ordered by exam session then set code then question number. Text is copied verbatim from the English text layer of the paper (content/source/cbse/), never reworded or corrected: line breaks are kept as \n and formulas are raw text (e.g. 'Pb(NO3)2'), which lib/formatFormula.ts renders with subscripts. Fields: id ('cbse10-<session>-<set code>-q<no>' from the first source); class ('10'); chapter_id; question_text (for mcq the stem only, otherwise the full question including sub-parts and any 'OR' alternative); marks (from the paper's section rules, or the printed marks for the 2026 paper); type ('mcq' | 'assertion_reason' | 'very_short' | 'short' | 'long' | 'case_based' — 2023 onward: 1 mark = mcq/assertion_reason, 2 = very_short, 3 = short, 5 = long, 4 = case_based; 2022 Term-2 papers call both their 2- and 3-mark sections 'short answer', so both are 'short', and their 4-mark questions are case_based); options (array of {label, text} exactly as printed, for mcq and assertion_reason only — assertion_reason options come from the shared instruction block printed above those questions; null otherwise or when unreadable); correct_option (mcq and assertion_reason only: the option label given as the answer in CBSE's official marking scheme for that set, matched by session + set code + question number, never by wording; null when no scheme covers the set or the scheme awards the mark to all candidates; when schemes for different sets of a merged question give different labels, correct_option holds the first and correct_option_variants lists every set's label as [{set_code, correct_option}], and the question is flagged); has_diagram (true when the paper shows a figure, apparatus diagram or drawn structural formula for the question; the image itself is not stored); source (array — one entry per paper/set the identical question appeared in within the same exam session: {folder, file, session, series, set_code, question_no}; set_code '31(B)' or '31(B)/S' is the visually-impaired paper); exam_pattern ('2022_term2' = 40-mark Term-2 papers, '2023_onward' = 80-mark full-syllabus papers); marking_points (all other types: the value points from CBSE's official marking scheme for that set as [{point, marks}], copied verbatim in scheme order including 'OR' branches and the alternative answers the scheme accepts; an {point: 'OR', marks: null} entry separates internal-choice branches, marks is null for unmarked text such as an 'Alternative answer' note, and point is null where the scheme awards marks for content drawn as graphics (a diagram, structure or equation) that is not in its text layer; point boundaries are inferred from where the scheme prints each mark, so a line can sit in the neighbouring point, but no text is reworded or added; null when no English scheme covers the set; when schemes for different sets of a merged question differ, marking_points holds the version whose marks add up and marking_points_variants lists every readable set's version as [{set_code, question_no, marking_points}], and the question is flagged); answer_source (where the answer came from: [{file, set_code, question_no, pages}] — file is under content/source/cbse/marking-schemes/extracted/, which is git-ignored with the rest of content/source/; absent when no scheme covers the question); flagged (true when the extracted text is known to be imperfect) and flag_reason (plain-English reason(s), '; '-separated, null when not flagged; reasons about the marking-scheme answer start with '[scheme]', e.g. marking points that do not add up to the question's marks, schemes that differ between sets, or scheme symbols that extracted as private-use characters — e.g. reaction arrow drawn as a graphic and missing, symbols extracted as garbage characters, words drawn as vector outlines and missing). A flagged question should be checked against the source page before it is shown to students.
